question: Deep diligence on a startup idea: an aquatic vegetation and algae-related cleanup service in Austin, Texas, starting with Lake Austin, Lady Bird Lake, nearby Highland Lakes, private ponds, HOAs, marinas, restaurants, and lakefront homeowners. Cover every requested diligence step: market size and demand; regulatory and permitting; environmental considerations; technology and equipment; seasonality and frequency; unit economics; competitive landscape; go-to-market; and expansion opportunity. Use CX research plus r-paper style evidence: current primary web sources for Austin/Texas market and regulation, plus papers/reviews/technical reports for hydrilla, invasive aquatic vegetation, cyanobacteria, mechanical harvesting, removal impacts, and water-quality management.
goal: Produce an investor-grade EIR diligence memo with cited findings, clear separation of user-provided facts, researched findings, informed inference, open questions, and an explicit investment recommendation of invest, watch, or pass. Include a Go/No-Go scorecard, low/base/high pilot economics, regulatory gating path, customer discovery targets, next 3 experiments, and a media/source appendix with useful images/video links for equipment, plants, algae examples, maps, and comparable service providers.
freshness: Current as of 2026-06-14. Verify recent Austin, LCRA, TPWD, City of Austin, algae, hydrilla, permitting, vendor pricing/lead-time, and competitor claims with up-to-date sources.
output_format: Comprehensive report with source-backed claims, contradiction checks, market map, regulatory checklist, technical/paper evidence section, media appendix, and investment verdict.
constraints: Treat founder input as unverified user-provided facts. Prefer primary sources: City of Austin, Austin Watershed Protection, TPWD, LCRA, TCEQ, Army Corps where relevant, equipment manufacturer pages, official contractor pages, official procurement/permit pages, papers/reviews/extension guidance. Do not treat unsupported TAM claims or vendor marketing as proof. Use exact dates for current algae/hydrilla status. Include chain search across subtopics and competitor/vendor discovery. If images/videos are found, record source URL, license/ownership caveat, and what the media shows; do not imply license rights. PatentsView credentials may be unavailable, so use USPTO/EPO/web fallback only if needed.

user_provided_facts: The idea is to launch a company providing aquatic vegetation and algae-related cleanup services for lakefront homeowners, restaurants, marinas, HOAs, and potentially municipalities in Austin.
Initial geographic focus: Lake Austin, Lady Bird Lake, nearby waterways, Lake Travis, Barton Creek, Colorado River segments, private ponds, golf-course ponds, and HOA lakes.

Core services under consideration: residential shoreline cleanup; commercial waterfront service; HOA/POA/neighborhood contracts; municipal and public-sector contracts; monitoring and prevention add-ons using drone/sonar/GIS, seasonal forecasting, nutrient-runoff recommendations, and disposal/composting partnerships.

The thesis is that this may be viable if positioned as recurring premium waterfront maintenance rather than one-time cleanup, but depends on permitting, environmental rules, liability, equipment utilization, disposal logistics, and willingness to pay privately.
startup_decision_lenses: Differentiation, moat, and barriers to entry
Customer personas, complaints, and purchase process
Market size, readiness, and Porter 5 Forces
Traction quality, growth engine, funnel, and testing opportunities
Team quality, gaps, and funding sufficiency

chain_objective: Research each diligence section deeply enough to support a sourced Notion report and investment verdict.
